fact: For positive integer m and any real a, m(1/m)^a=(1/m)^{a-1}.

fact: The reciprocals 1/m of positive integers become arbitrarily small: for every h>0, all sufficiently large positive m satisfy 0<1/m<h.
justification: Use exists_nat_gt in ℝ at 1/h (and, if necessary, at 0, or simply take the larger threshold). The real field has the required ordered semiring and Archimedean structures. For all larger m, reciprocal inequalities give the assertion. Together with the input N001 limit h^{a-1}→0, this verifies the displayed eventual scale qualification and arbitrarily small cover cost; it introduces no new analytical limit theorem.
